analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials thoughts on today ... 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: Industrials are down about 200bps while materials are up about 150bps, with materials matching broader market strength. Consumer and healthcare lead the market and energy is sharply lower.
Housing, airlines and autos are the subsectors higher on the screen. Data center, defense and aerospace are lower.
Factors are described as upside down: short interest is ripping and momentum is getting hit hard. The desk notes industrial short interest had its biggest move in 5 years.
ADP printed 86k vs. a 67k survey and ISM services came in essentially in line at 54.5 vs. 54.8.

AI / data center names fell the most. FIX, PWR, ETN and VRT are down 10-20% in large caps. The desk expects concerns about project delays, pushouts and moratoriums to continue near term. Dip-buying inquiries are coming in, but the desk sees zero conviction that the bottom is in.

Defense is down about 5% (LMT, LHX, NOC, RTX, GD). The desk thinks mitigating factors could get these moves bought: a clean quarter across the board, stockpiles being worked down given the geopolitical situation, the DoW push for volumes, and spending likely higher not lower near term.

Housing is up 5-7% depending on the name, with rates lower on growth concerns and oil lower. The desk sees this being good for rate-sensitive names and the consumer, and expects the move to continue near term. The reaction is more subdued in autos and airlines.
SWK is up 15%. Bull feedback centers on gross margins. Bear feedback is that pricing is negative and implied Q4 is double digits below consensus.

MLM is essentially flat, not reacting with the rest of rate-sensitive names. Pushback is that revenue growth is above EBITDA growth. Mix-adjusted pricing is mid-to-high single digits and in line, with debate on the mix impact.
EMR is up 1%, with muted feedback and outperformance as oil falls. The debate is whether underlying order growth is 14% in fiscal Q4 or something less, given some very long cycle orders.

WCC is down 12%. The desk cites data center exposure, ISM leverage (cyclicals getting hit, desk says it is risk off), distributor inflation-winner status (inflation expectations coming in) and crowding.
MOD is down 22%. The desk thinks the move is mostly macro, since other SMID AI names are down 15-20% and MOD had lower expectations into the print. The quarter missed and guidance was lowered.
Transports are weak broadly. UPS is higher, XPO lower, and the desk points to short crowding in CP and GXO, with KNX more owned.
The desk is asking for feedback on the impact on ag machinery (DE, AGCO, CNH) and other ag-related names (CTVA, ADM, BG).
Upcoming single-name focus after the close on 11/4: CF, CGNX, ITT, NTR. On 11/5 morning: APD, CMI, IBP, MAIR, PH, ROK, WMS. FAST October sales are due with a roughly 15% bogey.
